correctness.rationale: The scaled Ito Euler update induces exact symmetric nonnegative transfer T on the diagonal second moments, with the off-diagonal multiplier dominated by rho(T). The strict positivity of I-T is equivalent to a uniquely located root of AD(2-Ah)(2-Dh)-4a^2, producing the sharp h*. The explicit inverse of I-T yields invariant covariance; the exact positive residual h^2(A^2,D^2) proves strict inflation. Positive forcing and a nonnegative Perron eigenvector rule out finite-moment stationarity for all h at or above the boundary. Algebraic limits give inverse fourth-power amplitude stiffness and the optimal-scaling finite limit. Standalone rational tests replay these formulas; the proof is analytic.

value.rationale: The continuous-time optimal reversible-noise acceleration uses arbitrarily large noise amplitudes but the recently studied algorithm is implemented with finite Euler steps; determining how stability and sampling covariance behave is a motivated numerical-analysis gap. The closed sharp threshold tells exactly when long-run finite-variance sampling is feasible, the universal strict covariance inflation diagnoses systematic equilibrium bias, and the inverse-fourth-power perturbation amplitude law quantifies a severe previously unstated implementation cost. The classification covers a natural complete two-parameter benchmark, not an arbitrary table slice.
